name: Madai
title: Japheth's son and the ancestor of the Medes
summary: Madai was one of the sons of Japheth, who was the son of Noah. He is traditionally regarded as the ancestor of the Medes, the people who founded the Median Empire in ancient Iran. His name appears in the Bible's genealogies as part of the origins of nations after the flood.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Noah's genealogy
keyEvents.description: Madai is listed as one of Japheth's seven sons in the post-flood genealogy, which describes how the nations spread across the earth.

keyEvents.title: Table of Nations
keyEvents.description: In the Table of Nations in Genesis 10, it is described how Noah's descendants became various peoples and nations, and Madai is linked to the Medes who settled in northwestern Iran.

keyEvents.title: Repeated in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Madai is mentioned again in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles as one of Japheth's sons, confirming his place in Israel's historical tradition.

keyEvents.title: The Medes in a Prophetic Context
keyEvents.description: The Medes, who were traditionally regarded as descendants of Madai, play an important role in the Bible's prophecies, especially in Isaiah's prophecy about the fall of Babylon.

keyEvents.title: The Medes and the Fall of Babylon
keyEvents.description: The prophet Daniel describes how the Medo-Persian empire took power from Babylon, which is linked to Madai's descendants as a mighty people in world history.
